notes: IMPORTANT: as of 2026-08-07 DMEA's All-State page still posts only 2025-2026 materials (the 2025-2026 All-State Student Packet and Directors Packet). No 2026-27 audition materials, dates, or repertoire had been posted, so every program below is labeled season 2025-26 and must not be read as 2026-27. DMEA runs an All-State Junior Chorus (grades 7-8) and All-State Senior Choirs (grades 9-12, Treble and Mixed) alongside band, orchestra, jazz, and modern band ensembles.

organization.name: Delaware Music Educators Association
organization.description: DMEA is the Delaware state affiliate of NAfME. It administers the Delaware All-State ensembles, the Let's Make Music Festival, awards and scholarships, and a Young Composers Contest. All-State events are self-supporting, financed by audition and registration fees.

programs.name: All-State Junior Chorus
programs.description: DMEA's All-State choral ensemble for grades 7-8. Students audition in person, attend a regional reading rehearsal, and then a three-day rehearsal and concert event. Attendance at every event is mandatory for accepted students.

dates.title: Reading rehearsal
dates.description: New Castle County at Wilmington Friends; Kent/Sussex at Frederick Thomas Middle School. Weather date 2/7/26.

dates.title: All-State Junior Chorus event
dates.description: Daily 9am-4pm, with a 4pm concert. Rehearsals at Dover Middle School; concert at Dover High School.

requirements.title: Grade levels
requirements.description: All-State Junior Chorus is open to grades 7-8.

requirements.title: School ensemble enrollment
requirements.description: Each applicant must be enrolled in and a participating member in good standing of their school's, sister school's, or district's music ensemble for the entire current school year, corresponding to the All-State ensemble applied for. Choral applicants must be in their school's choral ensembles. Home-schooled students are eligible only if they are enrolled in and participate in a school ensemble that regularly rehearses and performs within the local public school district where they reside.

requirements.title: Director must be a NAfME/DMEA member
requirements.description: The music teacher signing the application must be the teacher of record for the qualifying ensemble and a current NAfME/DMEA member; membership is verified through the national affiliate. Students of non-member directors are not eligible to participate.

requirements.title: No known conflicts
requirements.description: Students with known conflicts that would preclude participation in any portion of the rehearsals or the event are not eligible to audition. Requests to miss any portion of a rehearsal or concert are not entertained.

requirements.title: Prepared audition piece
requirements.description: Music begins at m. 18 on the second half of beat 2; singers begin singing at m. 20 on the second half of beat 2 and sing to the end of the piece. Students sing their voice part along with a recording of the accompaniment. Sheet music is provided at the audition if needed. Memorization is not required.

requirements.title: Assessment criteria
requirements.description: Students are assessed on Tone Quality, Intonation, Pitch Accuracy, Rhythm & Tempo, Diction & Phrasing, and Range.

requirements.title: Sight-reading
requirements.description: The exercise starts on the tonic and contains only stepwise motion, is 4 measures long, does not exceed one octave in range, uses note values no shorter than eighth notes, and includes rests. Keys by part: Soprano F, Alto C, Tenor A-flat, Baritone E-flat. Solfege letters and numbers are printed below each note; students may sing on 'la' or any syllable or number without penalty and get 2 attempts.

requirements.title: Concert Black dress code
requirements.description: Students must wear conservative solid-black Concert Black attire with no prints, patterns, stripes, or dots. Dress/skirt outfits: knee length or longer, short or long sleeves only (no sleeveless), black stockings or tights, black dress shoes with low or no heel. Pant outfits: black dress pants, black long-sleeve dress shirt, black socks, black dress shoes, black belt. Sequins, rhinestones, hats, scarves, jeans, cargo/crop/yoga pants, sandals, flip flops, sneakers, and colored socks are not permitted. Students who do not meet the dress code are not allowed on the concert stage.

fees.description: An application fee of $20.00 is charged for each application. The fee may be paid by individuals, district, school, or booster organizations; if the district or school is paying, the Payment Form must be filed within one week after the deadline.

programs.name: All-State Senior Choirs (Treble and Mixed)
programs.description: DMEA's All-State choral program for grades 9-12, comprising a Treble Choir and a Mixed Choir. Singers audition in person from a single set of published requirements, attend a regional reading rehearsal, and perform at a three-day event.

dates.title: Reading rehearsal
dates.description: Kent/Sussex at Woodbridge High School; New Castle County at Concord High School. Weather date 2/17/26.

dates.title: All-State Senior Choirs event
dates.description: Daily 9am-4pm, with a 7pm concert. Held at Dover High School.

requirements.title: Grade levels
requirements.description: All-State Senior Choirs (Treble and Mixed) are open to grades 9-12.

requirements.title: School ensemble enrollment
requirements.description: Each applicant must be enrolled in and a participating member in good standing of their school's, sister school's, or district's choral ensemble for the entire current school year. Home-schooled students are eligible only if they are enrolled in and participate in a choral ensemble that regularly rehearses and performs within the local public school district where they reside.

requirements.title: Director must be a NAfME/DMEA member
requirements.description: The music teacher signing the application must be the teacher of record for the qualifying ensemble and a current NAfME/DMEA member. Students of non-member directors are not eligible to participate.

requirements.title: Prepared audition piece
requirements.description: Students learn the vocal part for which they wish to audition and sing measures 61 to the end (accompaniment begins at m. 57 at the piano interlude). Students audition with a track containing the other vocal parts but excluding the part being auditioned. DMEA supplies a PDF of the piece, IPA pronunciation and translation, rehearsal tracks, and audition tracks.

requirements.title: Prepared piece scoring
requirements.description: 0-9 points possible for each of: Tone, Pitch Accuracy, Rhythmic Accuracy, Dynamics, Phrasing, and Diction.

requirements.title: Sight-reading
requirements.description: Students prepare to sight read in the key of C, F, G, Eb, or D. The example begins and ends on the tonic and contains at least one leap of a 3rd or 4th and a dotted rhythm. A track provides a I-IV-V-I progression, the starting pitch, and a 4-beat click to establish tempo. Students sing a cappella using solfege or a neutral syllable and are assessed only on pitch and rhythmic accuracy (0-9 points each).

requirements.title: Concert Black dress code
requirements.description: Students must wear conservative solid-black Concert Black attire with no prints, patterns, stripes, or dots, per the All-State Operations Manual. Students who do not meet the dress code are not allowed on the concert stage.

repertoire.title: Sehnsucht, Op. 112 No. 1
repertoire.notes: 2025-2026 required Senior Choir audition piece; measures 61 to the end.
